scope: Rehabilitate City Hall Station on the Broad Street Line and 15th Street Station on the Market-Frankford Line (MFL) for full ADA compliance, improved safety and security, state of good repair (SGR), and reduced maintenance costs. The 15th Street Station rehab was completed in 2020.
amendment1_note: Cost increase from $98.53 million due to updated estimates and scheduling.

scope: Station enhancements, relocation, and construction at Coatesville, Parkesburg, and Downingtown.
Updated fare collection system, systemwide.

facility: Regional Rail Catenaries 30th Street Station Westbound
scope: Catenary replacement from 30th Street Station westbound to K and Zoo interlocking and Powelton Yard.
Replace aging Silverliner IV railcars to improve infrastructure, update vehicle specifications, and support the Reimagining Regional Rail initiative.
amendment1_note: Cost increase from $626.64 million due to rescoping from partial fleet replacement. The new amount accounts for all 230 rail cars.

scope: Upgrade underground pedestrian tunnel network that connects major transit stations beneath Center City, Philadelphia.
Expand train storage and improve access to the Paoli/Thorndale Line, reducing costs from non-revenue train movements.
Replace Market-Frankford Line M-4 railcars, including vehicle design, production, signal upgrades, and facility improvements at 69th Street and Bridge Street yards.
Program for overhauls, plus replacements at Ellen, Market, Park, Broad, Loudon, Caster, and Ranstead.
Upgrade Paoli Station with a new center high-level platform, elevators, ramps, ADA improvements, and supporting infrastructure changes to ensure multimodal access.
SGR improvements, including retaining wall construction and first and second phases of track work.
Track 2 upgrades and bidirectional signaling from Paoli to Overbrook.
Construct new intermodal station and extend Route 36 Trolley.
Bus stop and transit priority enhancements.
New tracks, bridges, power systems, signal and communication upgrades, tunnel overhauls, and coordination with city and utility agencies.
Acquire 130 new ADA-accessible trolleys and support their design, testing, operator training, and system integration.
Design and construction of a new trolley heavy maintenance facility and upgrade of existing facilities to support the new trolley fleet, improve reliability, and ensure ADA compliance.
Redesign trolley routes, implement new schedules and operations, and train staff to support the modernized fleet and improve system efficiency.
Improve trolley access for Title VI communities through extensions to Overbrook, Eastwick, and Upper Darby, supporting regional job growth and economic development.
New Intercity bus station to replace Filbert Street Bus Terminal.

facility: Mainline-Schuylkill Bridges, Interlockings, and Duct Bank
scope: Rehabilitate seven bridges and interlockings between Suburban Station and 30th Street Station.
amendment1_note: Decrease in YOE cost from $433.52 million due to additional engineering analysis. SEPTA has completed 15% of design and is performing a value engineering assessment.

scope: Reconfigure and upgrade Regional Rail stations at Marcus Hook, Willow Grove, Cornwells Heights, Jenkintown-Wyncote, and Villanova (Phase 2) to improve accessibility and service.
amendment1_note: Updated scope to advance funds for Bristol (Trenton Line) and Noble (West Trenton Line, design-only) Regional Rail. No cost change.

scope: ADA compliance of SEPTA stations by installing elevators and modernizing escalators.
Rehabilitate SEPTA’s headquarters with upgrades to electrical, HVAC, elevators, and life safety systems, along with space optimization to enhance efficiency and leasing potential.

facility: Zero Emission Bus (ZEB) Fleet Transition Facility Upgrades
scope: Full transition to zero-emission buses, including battery electric and fuel cell models, contingent on securing necessary infrastructure funding.
Rebuild and reconfigure key Regional Rail interlockings to enhance operational efficiency, including locations such as 16th Street, Broad, Wayne, and Schuylkill.
Replace and upgrade SEPTA’s aging Regional Rail radio system to improve portable coverage, close safety-critical gaps, and meet current AREMA and AAR standards.
Modernize the Regional Rail signal system, including upgrades to improve operational reliability for the train control systems.
Modernize the Norristown High Speed Line (NHSL) signal system to improve reliability, address SGR needs, and incorporate advanced train control technology.
Replace and install upgraded mobile video systems across SEPTA’s fleet, including inward-facing cameras on Regional Rail cars and crash-hardened recorders on buses.
Rehabilitate or replace aging bridges across the system to maintain an SGR, including structures on the Fox Chase, Lansdale/Doylestown, Media/Elwyn, Manayunk/Norristown, and West Trenton Lines.
amendment1_note: Cost increase from $166.1 million due to the inclusion of seven Chestnut Hill West Line Bridges.

scope: Replace vehicles and necessary infrastructure for the Norristown High Speed Line (NHSL).
Reconstruction of a key intersection and addition of a new connector road with a signal to improve traffic flow and reduce congestion near I-295 and NJ Turnpike Exit 6A.

Separate freight and passenger service through Norristown by constructing a dedicated freight track and rebuilding the Norristown Transportation Center with high platforms and full accessibility to enable reliable S Line operations.

facility: Coatesville Turnback: Interlocking and Pocket Track
scope: Construction of a turnback pocket track in Atglen to allow SEPTA trains to reverse off the main line west of Thorndale, improving operational flexibility on the Keystone Line.

facility: Paoli / Thorndale Line Station Upgrades (Phase 1 to Villanova)
scope: Upgrade of track, signals, overhead wire, and stations along the Amtrak-owned Paoli/Thorndale Line to improve reliability and accessibility, including construction of high platforms and full ADA access at 17 stations.

facility: Broad Street Line (BSL) Vehicle Replacement and Infrastructure
scope: Replace aging BSL railcars with modern trainsets and complete related signal and infrastructure upgrades to improve operational efficiency.
amendment1_note: Cost increase from $127 million due to full rescoping from preliminary infrastructure work, and shift from P1 to P1–4. Approximately $726.3 million is deferred after FY 2038.

scope: ADA compliance for BSL and MFL stations, including 11th Street, 34th Street, Bridgeport, Chinatown, Ellsworth-Federal, Erie, Fairmount, Hunting Park, Logan, Lombard-South, Snyder, Spring Garden, and Wyoming.
Ongoing replacement of SEPTA’s >1,000 buses, including the purchase of 247 hybrid diesel-electric buses
Construct a multilevel parking garage.
Rehabilitate the Chestnut Hill East Line from Wayne Junction to Chestnut Hill East, including track, bridge, signal, and power upgrades, along with station ADA improvements.
Rehabilitate the Chestnut Hill West Line from Lehigh Interlocking to Chestnut Hill West, including track, bridge, signal, and power upgrades, along with station ADA improvements.
Station will soon be closing; possible relocation to Engle/Townsend Street.
Restore service by extending Media/Wawa Line to West Chester Borough.
New fixed-guideway shuttle service connecting 30th Street Station, the new 30th Street District development, Mantua neighborhood, and the Philadelphia Zoo.
New SEPTA station on the Keystone Corridor between Malvern and Exton.
New Station on the Market-Frankford Line.
Restore service from Lansdale to Perkasie.
Transit connections to Bellwether District. Alignment is undetermined at this time.
Rail line extension from Hughes Park to King of Prussia Mall.
Transit extension from NRG Station to the Navy Yard.
Parking improvements at various Regional Rail Stations.

facility: Trunk Line Infrastructure, Fern Rock Layover, and Stations (Melrose and Elkins Park)
scope: Rehabilitate the Reading Main Line from 16th Street Junction to Carmel Interlocking, including track, bridge, signal, and power upgrades, station ADA improvements, and operational enhancements at Fern Rock.
Reconstruct and consolidate North Philadelphia and North Broad stations into a new regional intermodal hub to improve connectivity across SEPTA, Amtrak, and NJ Transit services.

facility: Airport Freight Separation and Eastwick Intermodal Station Phase 1
scope: Construct a separate freight track through Eastwick Station to eliminate conflicts with SEPTA’s Airport Line and enable more reliable service and high-level platform construction.

facility: Airport Double Track and Airport Tail Track
scope: Double track a key two-mile segment of the Airport Line and construct a tail track near the terminals to improve capacity, reliability, and service frequency to Philadelphia International Airport.
Construct a SEPTA flyover near 54th Street in West Philadelphia to eliminate conflicts with Amtrak and increase capacity and reliability on the Wilmington/Newark and Airport lines.

facility: Norristown Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Upgrade all Norristown Line stations with high platforms and accessible routes to improve speed and reliability; three are already in the CIP. Rehabilitate the full 14.6-mile line—track, bridges, signals, and power—for long-term performance.
Construct a flyover south of 16th Street Junction to fully separate S-Line trains from SEPTA’s Regional Rail trunk, reducing conflicts and improving reliability.

facility: Media/Wawa Line Station and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Rehabilitate the full 15.7-mile Media/Wawa Line with new track, signals, power, bridges, and drainage; construct high-level platforms at 12 stations and a grade-separated junction at Arsenal to improve reliability, ADA, and service frequency.
Extend double track from Elwyn to Lenni Yard to support frequent service on the Media/Wawa Line, requiring grading, bridge modifications, and crossover installation within available ROW.

facility: Major Grade Crossings Along the Media Wawa Line
scope: Grade-separate rail crossings and reconfigure nearby intersections at Morton and Secane stations to reduce traffic conflicts and improve safety on the Media/Wawa Line.

facility: Lansdale Doylestown Line Station and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Upgrade all stations on the Lansdale/Doylestown Line with full-length high platforms and accessible routes, and rehabilitate track, power, and signal infrastructure to improve reliability and reduce delays.

Reconfigure tracks and platforms at Lansdale Station to improve speeds, provide accessible platforms, and reduce freight conflicts, supporting more efficient and reliable service within the existing ROW.

Add double-track segments near 9th Street, New Britain, and Delaware Valley University to improve reliability and allow more frequent service on the Lansdale–Doylestown Line. Build new high-level platforms where needed; final track and station designs depend on further analysis. Add a second platform at Doylestown Station to support all-day two-way service—may require relocating train storage to Lansdale.
Develop a new yard and maintenance facility with crew reporting capabilities between Glenside and Lansdale to support expanded service. Location and scope to be determined through further analysis.

Support implementation of the Amtrak Keystone Master Plan in coordination with PennDOT and Amtrak. Includes new interlocking and pocket track west of Villanova to enable 15-minute service and ADA improvements, and new crossovers east of Ardmore to reduce conflicts between Amtrak and SEPTA trains.

Construct or rehabilitate the Stiles Flyover to reduce train conflicts between SEPTA and Amtrak and improve access to Overbrook Yard. Includes a new Cynwyd Line connection to the shop. Requires coordination with Amtrak and PennDOT, and construction over active tracks.

facility: Trenton Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Upgrade Trenton Line stations with full-length high platforms and accessible routes for faster, more reliable service. Rehabilitate track, bridges, and signals in coordination with Amtrak and the NEC Commission. Requires overnight work or temporary closures and joint planning on Amtrak ROW.

Upgrade Grundy Interlocking in coordination with Amtrak to improve operations and convert an existing unused siding into an electrified turnback pocket for SEPTA trains. Part of NEC Connect 2037; requires further alternatives analysis and interagency coordination.
Add a new southbound track connecting to Mantua Interlocking, eliminating a key bottleneck where SEPTA and Amtrak services currently merge, to improve reliability and capacity through this segment.

New yard and maintenance facility in Trenton—potentially in partnership with Amtrak or NJ Transit—would reduce long deadhead trips, improve operations on the Trenton Line, and support a new fleet; site location to be determined through further study.

facility: Warminster Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Fully rehabilitate the Warminster Line—upgrading track, power, signals, drainage, bridges, and crossings—and build high platforms with accessible routes at all stations to improve reliability, speed, and accessibility.

Extend double track from Ardsley through Roslyn and expand the siding through Willow Grove, rebuild affected stations with high platforms, and add a second platform at Warminster Station to eliminate operational constraints.

facility: West Trenton Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Fully rebuild the West Trenton Line—modernizing track, power, signals, bridges, drainage, and crossings—and construct high platforms with accessible routes at all stations to improve reliability, speed, and accessibility.

facility: Wilmington/Newark Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Rehabilitate track, signals, bridges, and overhead wire on the Wilmington/Newark Line and rebuild 14 stations with high-level platforms and accessible routes to improve reliability, passenger experience, and service frequency.

Add a third track through the single-track segments south of Claymont and Wilmington to separate SEPTA service from Amtrak, enabling more frequent trains and reducing conflicts, with further study and coordination needed.

Build a turnback pocket off the Northeast Corridor near Marcus Hook station, with upgraded signals at Hook Interlocking to improve capacity by allowing trains to lay over off the mainline, while studying other alternatives.

Build a new yard and shop in Delaware with maintenance and crew facilities to reduce deadhead moves and support new fleet operations, with the location to be determined through further study and requiring acquisition of a suitable parcel.

facility: Cynwyd Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
scope: Rehabilitate the Cynwyd Line’s aging track, bridges, power, and signals, and add a second track plus two high-level platforms at Cynwyd station to improve reliability, accessibility, and capacity, with other alternatives to be studied.

facility: Roberts Yard and Powelton Yard Reconstruction
scope: Rebuild Roberts and Powelton yards with modern maintenance and crew facilities to accommodate future fleet needs.
New transit service within Philadelphia.
Rail Line Extension from Thorndale to Atglen.
New high-capacity transit along Roosevelt Boulevard.
